```markdown
<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

192	
193	**练习 1**：为什么 `apply_chat_template` 必须传 `tokenize=False`，而不能像 transformers 路径那样传 `tokenize=True`？
194	
195	**答案**：`tokenize=True` 会直接产出 `input_ids` 和 `pixel_values` 等**已经预处理完**的张量，那是给 `model.generate` 用的；而 vLLM 引擎要求输入是「文本串 + 原始视觉数据」，它要在引擎内部自行完成 tokenization 与视觉展开。若传 `tokenize=True`，产出对 vLLM 无从递交给引擎，且 `tokenize=False` 时每图仅留一个占位符，正适合让 vLLM 按实际视觉 token 数展开。

201	### 4.2 多模态数据字典 multi_modal_data
202	
203	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
204	
205	`multi_modal_data` 是 vLLM 定义的多模态输入挂载点：一个字典，键是模态名（`'image'`、`'video'`），值是**已经解码并缩放好的视觉数据列表**。vLLM 收到后，会在引擎内部把它们与 prompt 里的占位符一一对应，展开成真正的视觉 token 送入视觉编码器。
206	
207	它与 `prompt` 的分工是：**prompt 描述「视觉内容出现在对话的什么位置、有几份」，multi_modal_data 提供「视觉内容本身」**。
208	
209	图像侧的值是 PIL `Image.Image` 对象列表（`process_vision_info` 的 `fetch_image` 产出），视频侧的值则可能是张量或「张量 + 元数据」元组（见 4.3 节）。
210	
211	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
212	
213	一条含 1 图 1 视频的请求，数据流如下：
214	
215	```text
216	messages
217	  ├── apply_chat_template(tokenize=False) ──► prompt 串: "...<|image_pad|>...<|video_pad|>..."
218	  └── process_vision_info(...)
219	        ├── image_inputs = [PIL 图]        ──► mm_data['image'] = [PIL 图]
220	        └── video_inputs = [(张量, 元数据)] ──► mm_data['video'] = [(张量, 元数据)]
221	
222	vLLM 引擎内部: 按占位符顺序取 mm_data 中的数据 → 视觉编码 → 展开进序列 → 解码生成
223	```
224	
225	视觉 token 数量与图像宽高的关系（承接 u3-l1）：图像被 32×32 空间压缩，视频再叠加 2× 时间压缩。对缩放后为 \(H' \times W'\) 的单帧，\(T\) 帧视频的视觉 token 数为
226	
227	\[
228	N_{\text{video}} = \frac{H'}{32} \times \frac{W'}{32} \times \frac{T}{2}
229	\]
230	
231	这个数量不由你的脚本计算，而由 vLLM 引擎按传入张量的实际尺寸展开——你的脚本只负责把尺寸控制好（元素级 `min_pixels`/`max_pixels` 或 processor 的 `size` 预算）。

258	### 4.3 video_metadata 解包与 mm_processor_kwargs 传参
259	
260	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
261	
262	这是本讲最微妙也最容易踩坑的模块，涉及三件事：
263	
264	1. **`return_video_metadata=True` 改变了 `video_inputs` 的形态**。开关关闭时，`video_inputs` 是 `[视频张量, ...]`；开关打开时，每个视频变成 `(视频张量, video_metadata)` **元组**，整个 `video_inputs` 变成元组列表。`video_metadata` 记录了原视频的 `fps`、`frames_indices`（采样帧在原视频中的帧号）、`total_num_frames` 等时间档案（详见 u2-l4）——因为视频张量经过抽帧与缩放后，时间信息全部丢失，必须由 metadata 随帧携带，才能支撑 Qwen3-VL 的「文本-时间戳对齐」。
265	2. **`mm_processor_kwargs` 的核心内容是 `do_sample_frames=False`**。`qwen-vl-utils` 在库内**已经完成了帧采样**（按 `fps` 或 `nframes` 抽帧），如果引擎内部的处理器再采样一次，帧数就会错一倍。这个开关告诉处理器「帧已采好，别再动」。
266	3. **vLLM 路径与 transformers 路径的解包方式不同**。vLLM 直接收元组列表；transformers 手动调用 processor 时必须先 `zip(*)` 拆开再分别传参。这是两条路径最大的写法差异。
267	
268	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
269	
270	`process_vision_info` 内部如何构造 `video_kwargs`（这是 `mm_processor_kwargs` 的直接来源）：
271	
272	```text
273	video_kwargs = {'do_sample_frames': False}          # 恒有：帧已在库内采样完
274	if not return_video_metadata:                       # 仅 Qwen2.5-VL 兼容分支
275	    video_kwargs.update({'fps': video_sample_fps_list})
276	```
277	
278	于是形成清晰的版本分工：
279	
280	- **Qwen3-VL**（`return_video_metadata=True`）：`video_kwargs = {'do_sample_frames': False}`，时间信息走 metadata；
281	- **Qwen2.5-VL 兼容模式**（`return_video_metadata=False`）：`video_kwargs` 额外带 `fps` 列表，时间信息靠 T-RoPE 的 fps 重建。
282	
283	两条路径的视频传参对比：
284	
285	```text
286	vLLM 路径（本讲）:
287	    mm_data['video'] = [(张量1, 元数据1), (张量2, 元数据2), ...]   # 元组列表整体直传
288	    mm_processor_kwargs = {'do_sample_frames': False}
289	
290	transformers 路径（对比, README "Process Videos" 示例）:
291	    videos, video_metadatas = zip(*videos)   # 手动拆元组
292	    videos, video_metadatas = list(videos), list(video_metadatas)
293	    processor(text=text, videos=videos, video_metadata=video_metadatas,
294	              do_resize=False, **video_kwargs)
295	```

357	### 4.4 引擎初始化与 SamplingParams
358	
359	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
360	
361	准备好请求字典后，还差两块拼图：
362	
363	- **`LLM(...)`**：离线推理引擎对象。构造时完成权重加载、KV 缓存池分配，关键参数围绕「并行度」与「显存」。
364	- **`SamplingParams`**：采样参数。决定「贪心还是随机」「最多生成几个 token」等解码行为，与视觉输入无关，但多模态长输入下 `max_tokens` 要给足。
365	
366	最后 `llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params=...)` 把请求列表整批送入引擎，返回与输入等长的输出列表，每项的 `output.outputs[0].text` 就是生成文本。注意与 transformers 的一个差异：**vLLM 返回的只有新生成部分，不需要像 transformers 那样裁剪输入前缀**。
367	
368	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
369	
370	```text
371	引擎初始化
372	  os.environ['VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD'] = 'spawn'   # 多卡 worker 用 spawn 启动
373	  tensor_parallel_size = torch.cuda.device_count()        # 未指定时默认用满全部 GPU
374	  llm = LLM(model=..., tensor_parallel_size=..., gpu_memory_utilization=..., seed=0)
375	
376	批量推理
377	  inputs = [prepare_inputs_for_vllm(m, processor) for m in all_messages]  # 每条请求一个字典
378	  outputs = llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params=SamplingParams(...))
379	  for output in outputs:
380	      text = output.outputs[0].text        # 直接是新生成文本，无需裁剪
381	```
382	
383	其中「张量并行」指把单层权重切到多卡上并行计算，是比数据并行更细粒度的多卡协作方式，适合单卡放不下的大模型。
384	
385	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
386	
387	**引擎初始化——web 演示版**：
388

393	[README.md:994-995](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L994-L995) —— 脚本开头同样设置 `spawn` 环境变量，说明这是离线推理的标准前奏。

397	**请求构造与批量推理**：
398	
399	[README.md:1048-1051](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L1048-L1051) —— 批量的本质就是一个列表推导：对每份 messages 各调用一次 `prepare_inputs_for_vllm`，得到请求字典列表。想跑多少条就放多少份 messages。

401	[README.md:1061-1066](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L1061-L1066) —— 官方示例的 `SamplingParams`：`temperature=0`（贪心解码，评测首选，保证可复现）、`max_tokens=1024`、`top_k=-1`（不截断候选集）、`stop_token_ids=[]`（不额外设停止 token）。对照 [README.md:1142-1164](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L1142-L1164) 的官方评测超参可知产品级配置更细：Instruct 档用 `temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.5`，Thinking 档用 `temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, presence_penalty=0` 且 `out_seq_length=40960`——思考型模型要留足输出长度。

405	#### 4.4.4 代码实践
406	
407	1. **实践目标**：对比贪心与采样两种 `SamplingParams` 对同一输入的输出稳定性。
408	2. **操作步骤**：在综合实践（第 5 节）的脚本中准备两组参数——`SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256)` 与 `SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, max_tokens=256, seed=1234)`——对同一张图各跑两次推理。

413	
414	**练习 1**：web 演示中 `--tensor-parallel-size` 不传时的默认行为是什么？为什么这个默认值是合理的？
415	
416	**答案**：默认取 `torch.cuda.device_count()`，即用满当前进程可见的全部 GPU 作为张量并行组（web_demo_mm.py 第 57-60 行定义参数、第 72-74 行实现默认值）。对演示场景而言，单卡能放下就用 1 卡，多卡则自动分摊权重，用户无需关心机器拓扑。
417	
418	**练习 2**：transformers 推理要用 `out_ids[len(in_ids):]` 裁剪输出，vLLM 需要吗？
419	
420	**答案**：不需要。transformers 的 `model.generate` 返回「输入 + 新生成」拼接后的完整 id 序列，所以要裁剪前缀；vLLM 的 `output.outputs[0].text` 只包含新生成文本（web_demo_mm.py 第 213-217 行直接取 `completion.text` 使用即是佐证）。

422	**练习 3**：为什么 235B-A22B 示例要加 `mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`，而 2B 示例不需要？
423	
424	**答案**：该参数控制视觉编码器在张量并行下的切分方式：大模型并行度高时，按数据切分（每卡各处理一部分图像）比按张量切分更省显存与通信。2B 模型通常单卡即可放下（`tensor_parallel_size=1`），不存在编码器切分问题，无需该参数。详见 README 部署一节引用的 vLLM 社区指南。

426	## 5. 综合实践：批量离线推理脚本（2 张图 + 1 个视频）

429	
430	**实践目标**：独立写出自己的第一个 Qwen3-VL + vLLM 离线推理脚本。

432	**操作步骤**：

435	
436	```bash
437	pip install "transformers>=4.57.0" "vllm>=0.11.0" qwen-vl-utils==0.0.14 accelerate

439	
440	2. 编写 `offline_infer.py`（示例代码，参照 [README.md:986-1080](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L986-L1080) 官方示例改写）：
441	
442	```python
443	# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
444	import os
445	import torch
446	from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info
447	from transformers import AutoProcessor
448	from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
449	
450	os.environ['VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD'] = 'spawn'
451	
452	IMG1 = "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-VL/assets/demo.jpeg"
453	IMG2 = "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen2-VL/assets/demo.jpeg"  # 换成你自己的第二张图

455	
456	
457	def prepare_inputs_for_vllm(messages, processor):
458	    """三件套: prompt + multi_modal_data + mm_processor_kwargs"""
459	    text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
460	    image_inputs, video_inputs, video_kwargs = process_vision_info(
461	        messages,
462	        image_patch_size=processor.image_processor.patch_size,  # 动态读取, Qwen3-VL 为 16
463	        return_video_kwargs=True,
464	        return_video_metadata=True,   # 视频 -> (张量, metadata) 元组列表
465	    )
466	    print(f"video_kwargs: {video_kwargs}")   # 预期 {'do_sample_frames': False}
467	
468	    mm_data = {}
469	    if image_inputs is not None:
470	        mm_data['image'] = image_inputs      # PIL 列表直传
471	    if video_inputs is not None:
472	        mm_data['video'] = video_inputs      # 元组列表直传, 由 vLLM 解包
473	    return {
474	        'prompt': text,
475	        'multi_modal_data': mm_data,
476	        'mm_processor_kwargs': video_kwargs, # 防止引擎内二次抽帧
477	    }
478	
479	
480	if __name__ == '__main__':
481	    ckpt = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct"
482	    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ckpt)
483	
484	    all_messages = [
485	        [  # 请求 1: 单图
486	            {"role": "user", "content": [
487	                {"type": "image", "image": IMG1},
488	                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
489	            ]},
490	        ],
491	        [  # 请求 2: 单图
492	            {"role": "user", "content": [
493	                {"type": "image", "image": IMG2},
494	                {"type": "text", "text": "What is in this image?"},
495	            ]},
496	        ],
497	        [  # 请求 3: 视频
498	            {"role": "user", "content": [
499	                {"type": "video", "video": VID},
500	                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."},
501	            ]},
502	        ],
503	    ]
504	
505	    inputs = [prepare_inputs_for_vllm(m, processor) for m in all_messages]
506	
507	    llm = LLM(model=ckpt, tensor_parallel_size=min(1, torch.cuda.device_count()), seed=0)
508	    sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=512)
509	
510	    outputs = llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params=sampling_params)
511	    for i, output in enumerate(outputs):
512	        print("=" * 40)
513	        print(f"[{i}] prompt 长度: {len(output.prompt_token_ids)} tokens")
514	        print(f"[{i}] 生成文本: {output.outputs[0].text}")
515	```

525	
526	**预期结果**：三段与各图/视频内容相符的描述文本；图像请求的 `mm_data` 只有 `'image'` 键。全流程显存不足以运行 2B 模型时，可改用官方 Docker 镜像（见 [README.md:1167-1173](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L1167-L1173)）。**本实践未在编写本讲义时实际运行，待本地验证。**

528	## 6. 本讲小结

530	- `prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 是仓库级标准模式，在 web 演示、README 示例与全部五个评测目录中逐行同构地出现，核心是三步：`apply_chat_template(tokenize=False)` 渲染文本 → `process_vision_info` 解码视觉素材 → 组装三件套字典。

# vLLM 离线推理与 prepare_inputs_for_vllm 模式

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 独立实现 `prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 函数——这是本仓库中反复出现的一段「样板代码」，出现在 web 演示、README 示例和全部五个评测脚本中。
2. 准确说出 vLLM 离线推理输入的三个字段 `prompt`、`multi_modal_data`、`mm_processor_kwargs` 各自承担什么职责。
3. 掌握视频输入的特殊处理：`return_video_metadata=True` 时返回的 `(视频张量, video_metadata)` 元组列表如何传给 vLLM，以及 `do_sample_frames=False` 这个开关为什么必须传。
4. 会配置 vLLM 的 `LLM` 引擎参数与 `SamplingParams` 采样参数，并用 `llm.generate` 完成一次批量离线推理。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 vLLM 是什么

vLLM 是一个高性能推理引擎。相比直接用 transformers 的 `model.generate`，它通过两項核心技术大幅提升吞吐：

- **PagedAttention**：像操作系统管理内存页一样管理 KV 缓存，避免为每条请求预留整块显存。
- **连续批处理（continuous batching）**：新请求随时插入、完成的请求随时退出，GPU 始终满载。

本仓库 README 明确推荐用 vLLM 部署 Qwen3-VL，并要求 `vllm>=0.11.0`（低于该版本不支持 Qwen3-VL）。

### 2.2 离线推理 vs 在线服务

vLLM 有两种用法，本讲只讲前者：

| 方式 | 入口 | 适用场景 | 对应讲义 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **离线推理（offline）** | Python 里 `from vllm import LLM`，直接调用 `llm.generate(...)` | 批量跑数据、评测、一次性任务 | 本讲 |
| **在线服务（serving）** | 命令行 `vllm serve ...` 起一个 OpenAI 兼容 HTTP 服务 | 产品化 API 服务 | 下一讲 u3-l3 |

「离线」不是指断网，而是指**不起网络服务、在脚本进程内直接推理**。单元六的全部评测脚本（MMMU、VideoMME、ODinW-13 等）用的都是离线方式。

### 2.3 为什么 vLLM 需要手动准备多模态输入

回顾上一讲（u3-l1）的 transformers 路径：`processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=True, ...)` 一步就把 messages 变成了带 `pixel_values`、`image_grid_thw` 的张量字典。**processor 帮你做了所有事**。

vLLM 路径则把职责拆开：

- 你的脚本负责：把视觉内容从 messages 里**真正解码出来**（下载图片、解码视频帧、按像素预算缩放）；
- vLLM 引擎负责：接收文本 prompt 和现成的图像/视频张量，在引擎内部调用模型自带的多模态预处理器，把占位符展开成真正的视觉 token，再完成前向与解码。

于是就有了那个问题：谁来「真正解码」？答案就是 `qwen-vl-utils` 的 `process_vision_info`——这正是单元二花了四讲精读的库在此处派上用场。README 中也专门引用了 vLLM 官方多模态输入文档（见 [README.md:856-868](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L856-L868)）。

### 2.4 三个字段的契约预告

`llm.generate` 接收一个字典列表，每个字典描述一条请求：

```text
{
  'prompt':               渲染好的文本提示串（视觉位置只留占位符）
  'multi_modal_data':     {'image': [PIL图...], 'video': [视频...]} 现成的视觉数据
  'mm_processor_kwargs':  传给引擎内部处理器的关键字参数（如 do_sample_frames）
}
```

记住这张「三件套」卡片，下面逐个拆解。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 角色 |
| --- | --- |
| [web_demo_mm.py](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py) | Gradio 网页演示，其中的 `_prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 是该模式最紧凑的实现，vLLM 双后端加载逻辑也在其中 |
| [README.md](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md) | 「Offline Inference」一节给出完整的可运行 vLLM 示例脚本，是本讲的权威参照 |
| [qwen-vl-utils/src/qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/qwen-vl-utils/src/qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py) | `process_vision_info` 的实现，决定了三个返回值（尤其 `video_kwargs`）的确切内容 |
| [evaluation/mmmu/run_mmmu.py](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/evaluation/mmmu/run_mmmu.py) | MMMU 评测脚本，逐行复用了同一模式，证明它是仓库级的「标准写法」 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 输入准备函数：prepare_inputs_for_vllm

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 不是 vLLM 库的 API，而是**本仓库自己约定的一个辅助函数名**：输入标准 messages 和 processor，输出 vLLM `llm.generate` 需要的那条请求字典。它解决的问题是：**把「对话 + 视觉素材」翻译成「文本 prompt + 现成张量 + 处理器开关」三部分**。

这个函数在仓库里出现了至少 7 次，写法几乎逐行相同：

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

函数只有三步：

```text
输入: messages（含 image/video 元素的对话）, processor

第 1 步  渲染文本
    text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    # tokenize=False：只产出字符串，视觉位置仅保留一个 <|image_pad|>/<|video_pad|> 占位符

第 2 步  解码视觉素材
    image_inputs, video_inputs, video_kwargs = process_vision_info(
        messages,
        image_patch_size=processor.image_processor.patch_size,   # Qwen3-VL 为 16
        return_video_kwargs=True,                                # 额外返回 video_kwargs
        return_video_metadata=True                               # 视频变为 (张量, metadata) 元组
    )

第 3 步  组装三件套字典并返回
    {'prompt': text, 'multi_modal_data': mm_data, 'mm_processor_kwargs': video_kwargs}
```

注意一个关键细节：第 1 步与第 2 步**遍历的是同一份 messages**。`apply_chat_template` 数出「有几个视觉元素、各在哪个位置」来放置占位符；`process_vision_info` 按 messages 中出现的顺序产出视觉数据。两边顺序天然对齐，vLLM 才能把第 i 个占位符对应到第 i 份视觉数据。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看最紧凑的 web 演示版本：

[web_demo_mm.py:178-198](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/web_demo_mm.py#L178-L198) —— `_prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 完整实现：

```python
def _prepare_inputs_for_vllm(messages, processor):
    """Prepare inputs for vLLM inference"""
    text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    image_inputs, video_inputs, video_kwargs = process_vision_info(
        messages,
        image_patch_size=processor.image_processor.patch_size,
        return_video_kwargs=True,
        return_video_metadata=True
    )

    mm_data = {}
    if image_inputs is not None:
        mm_data['image'] = image_inputs
    if video_inputs is not None:
        mm_data['video'] = video_inputs

    return {
        'prompt': text,
        'multi_modal_data': mm_data,
        'mm_processor_kwargs': video_kwargs
    }
```

逐段说明：

- `tokenize=False`：只渲染出字符串。上一讲（u3-l1）讲过，此时每张图在串里只留一个 `<|image_pad|>` 占位 token；真正的视觉 token 数量由 vLLM 引擎内部按图像实际宽高展开。
- `image_patch_size=processor.image_processor.patch_size`：从 processor 动态读取 patch 边长（Qwen3-VL 为 16）。这是单元二强调过的最佳实践——**不要硬编码 16**，这样同一段代码也能服务 patch 为 14 的 Qwen2.5-VL。
- `return_video_kwargs=True` 与 `return_video_metadata=True`：两个开关同时打开，含义见 4.3 节。
- `mm_data` 只在对应输入非 `None` 时才填键：纯图请求就不会有 `'video'` 键，纯文本请求 `mm_data` 是空字典。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `apply_chat_template` 必须传 `tokenize=False`，而不能像 transformers 路径那样传 `tokenize=True`？

**答案**：`tokenize=True` 会直接产出 `input_ids` 和 `pixel_values` 等**已经预处理完**的张量，那是给 `model.generate` 用的；而 vLLM 引擎要求输入是「文本串 + 原始视觉数据」，它要在引擎内部自行完成 tokenization 与视觉展开。若传 `tokenize=True`，产出对 vLLM 无从递交给引擎，且 `tokenize=False` 时每图仅留一个占位符，正适合让 vLLM 按实际视觉 token 数展开。

**练习 2**：如果把 `image_patch_size=14`（Qwen2.5-VL 的值）误传给 Qwen3-VL，会发生什么？

**答案**：不会报错，但 `smart_resize` 会按 patch=14 的对齐因子（28）而非 32 来缩放图像，导致图像宽高不再是 32 的倍数，视觉 token 网格被算错，模型可能表现出细微的性能下降。这就是要从 `processor.image_processor.patch_size` 动态读取、而不是硬编码的原因（见单元二 u2-l1）。

### 4.2 多模态数据字典 multi_modal_data

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`multi_modal_data` 是 vLLM 定义的多模态输入挂载点：一个字典，键是模态名（`'image'`、`'video'`），值是**已经解码并缩放好的视觉数据列表**。vLLM 收到后，会在引擎内部把它们与 prompt 里的占位符一一对应，展开成真正的视觉 token 送入视觉编码器。

它与 `prompt` 的分工是：**prompt 描述「视觉内容出现在对话的什么位置、有几份」，multi_modal_data 提供「视觉内容本身」**。

图像侧的值是 PIL `Image.Image` 对象列表（`process_vision_info` 的 `fetch_image` 产出），视频侧的值则可能是张量或「张量 + 元数据」元组（见 4.3 节）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一条含 1 图 1 视频的请求，数据流如下：

```text
messages
  ├── apply_chat_template(tokenize=False) ──► prompt 串: "...<|image_pad|>...<|video_pad|>..."
  └── process_vision_info(...)
        ├── image_inputs = [PIL 图]        ──► mm_data['image'] = [PIL 图]
        └── video_inputs = [(张量, 元数据)] ──► mm_data['video'] = [(张量, 元数据)]

vLLM 引擎内部: 按占位符顺序取 mm_data 中的数据 → 视觉编码 → 展开进序列 → 解码生成
```

视觉 token 数量与图像宽高的关系（承接 u3-l1）：图像被 32×32 空间压缩，视频再叠加 2× 时间压缩。对缩放后为 \(H' \times W'\) 的单帧，\(T\) 帧视频的视觉 token 数为

\[
N_{\text{video}} = \frac{H'}{32} \times \frac{W'}{32} \times \frac{T}{2}
\]

这个数量不由你的脚本计算，而由 vLLM 引擎按传入张量的实际尺寸展开——你的脚本只负责把尺寸控制好（元素级 `min_pixels`/`max_pixels` 或 processor 的 `size` 预算）。

### 4.3 video_metadata 解包与 mm_processor_kwargs 传参

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

这是本讲最微妙也最容易踩坑的模块，涉及三件事：

1. **`return_video_metadata=True` 改变了 `video_inputs` 的形态**。开关关闭时，`video_inputs` 是 `[视频张量, ...]`；开关打开时，每个视频变成 `(视频张量, video_metadata)` **元组**，整个 `video_inputs` 变成元组列表。`video_metadata` 记录了原视频的 `fps`、`frames_indices`（采样帧在原视频中的帧号）、`total_num_frames` 等时间档案（详见 u2-l4）——因为视频张量经过抽帧与缩放后，时间信息全部丢失，必须由 metadata 随帧携带，才能支撑 Qwen3-VL 的「文本-时间戳对齐」。
2. **`mm_processor_kwargs` 的核心内容是 `do_sample_frames=False`**。`qwen-vl-utils` 在库内**已经完成了帧采样**（按 `fps` 或 `nframes` 抽帧），如果引擎内部的处理器再采样一次，帧数就会错一倍。这个开关告诉处理器「帧已采好，别再动」。
3. **vLLM 路径与 transformers 路径的解包方式不同**。vLLM 直接收元组列表；transformers 手动调用 processor 时必须先 `zip(*)` 拆开再分别传参。这是两条路径最大的写法差异。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`process_vision_info` 内部如何构造 `video_kwargs`（这是 `mm_processor_kwargs` 的直接来源）：

```text
video_kwargs = {'do_sample_frames': False}          # 恒有：帧已在库内采样完
if not return_video_metadata:                       # 仅 Qwen2.5-VL 兼容分支
    video_kwargs.update({'fps': video_sample_fps_list})
```

于是形成清晰的版本分工：

- **Qwen3-VL**（`return_video_metadata=True`）：`video_kwargs = {'do_sample_frames': False}`，时间信息走 metadata；
- **Qwen2.5-VL 兼容模式**（`return_video_metadata=False`）：`video_kwargs` 额外带 `fps` 列表，时间信息靠 T-RoPE 的 fps 重建。

两条路径的视频传参对比：

```text
vLLM 路径（本讲）:
    mm_data['video'] = [(张量1, 元数据1), (张量2, 元数据2), ...]   # 元组列表整体直传
    mm_processor_kwargs = {'do_sample_frames': False}

transformers 路径（对比, README "Process Videos" 示例）:
    videos, video_metadatas = zip(*videos)   # 手动拆元组
    videos, video_metadatas = list(videos), list(video_metadatas)
    processor(text=text, videos=videos, video_metadata=video_metadatas,
              do_resize=False, **video_kwargs)
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

[qwen-vl-utils/src/qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py:528-530](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/qwen-vl-utils/src/qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py#L528-L530) —— `video_kwargs` 的构造现场：第 528 行先放入 `do_sample_frames: False`；第 529-530 行仅在 `return_video_metadata=False`（Qwen2.5-VL 向后兼容分支）时追加 `fps` 列表。这解释了为什么 Qwen3-VL 模式下打印 `video_kwargs` 只会看到一个键。

[qwen-vl-utils/src/qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py:517-520](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/qwen-vl-utils/src/qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py#L517-L520) —— 视频元素的解码入口：对每个 video 元素调用 `fetch_video(..., return_video_metadata=return_video_metadata)`，返回值直接 `append` 进 `video_inputs`。当开关为 True 时，`fetch_video` 返回的就是 `(视频输入, 实际采样率)` 二元组、且其中的视频输入本身又是 `(张量, metadata)`——所以 `video_inputs` 最终是元组的列表，这正是 4.2 节 `mm_data['video']` 直传的形态。

[README.md:643-651](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L643-L651) —— transformers 路径的「手动解包」对照组：第 643-645 行用 `zip(*videos)` 把元组列表拆成 `videos` 与 `video_metadatas` 两个列表，第 651 行分别以 `videos=` 与 `video_metadata=` 传给 processor，同时传 `do_resize=False` 和 `**video_kwargs`。**注意 README 在这段代码注释里明确写了 "split the videos and according metadatas"**——这一步在 transformers 路径必须手动做，而 vLLM 路径（web_demo 与离线示例）直接把 `video_inputs` 塞进 `mm_data['video']`，解包由 vLLM 引擎内部完成。

[README.md:965-975](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L965-L975) —— 在线服务场景下的同类机制佐证：官方注释说明默认 `fps=2`、`do_sample_frames=True`（由服务端采样），可通过请求体 `extra_body={"mm_processor_kwargs": {"fps": 2, "do_sample_frames": True}}` 覆盖。可见 `do_sample_frames` 是贯穿离线与在线的同一个处理器开关：**谁来采样，谁就把开关置 False**——离线路径采样发生在 `qwen-vl-utils`，故传 False。

### 4.4 引擎初始化与 SamplingParams

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

准备好请求字典后，还差两块拼图：

- **`LLM(...)`**：离线推理引擎对象。构造时完成权重加载、KV 缓存池分配，关键参数围绕「并行度」与「显存」。
- **`SamplingParams`**：采样参数。决定「贪心还是随机」「最多生成几个 token」等解码行为，与视觉输入无关，但多模态长输入下 `max_tokens` 要给足。

最后 `llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params=...)` 把请求列表整批送入引擎，返回与输入等长的输出列表，每项的 `output.outputs[0].text` 就是生成文本。注意与 transformers 的一个差异：**vLLM 返回的只有新生成部分，不需要像 transformers 那样裁剪输入前缀**。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
引擎初始化
  os.environ['VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD'] = 'spawn'   # 多卡 worker 用 spawn 启动
  tensor_parallel_size = torch.cuda.device_count()        # 未指定时默认用满全部 GPU
  llm = LLM(model=..., tensor_parallel_size=..., gpu_memory_utilization=..., seed=0)

批量推理
  inputs = [prepare_inputs_for_vllm(m, processor) for m in all_messages]  # 每条请求一个字典
  outputs = llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params=SamplingParams(...))
  for output in outputs:
      text = output.outputs[0].text        # 直接是新生成文本，无需裁剪
```

其中「张量并行」指把单层权重切到多卡上并行计算，是比数据并行更细粒度的多卡协作方式，适合单卡放不下的大模型。

**答案**：默认取 `torch.cuda.device_count()`，即用满当前进程可见的全部 GPU 作为张量并行组（web_demo_mm.py 第 57-60 行定义参数、第 72-74 行实现默认值）。对演示场景而言，单卡能放下就用 1 卡，多卡则自动分摊权重，用户无需关心机器拓扑。

**操作步骤**：

1. 安装依赖（版本要求来自 [README.md:856-868](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L856-L868)）：

2. 编写 `offline_infer.py`（示例代码，参照 [README.md:986-1080](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/blob/96588727e44c78b25ba03ea03b8e12f7e64fd0da/README.md#L986-L1080) 官方示例改写）：

```python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import os
import torch
from qwen_vl_utils import process_vision_info
from transformers import AutoProcessor
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

os.environ['VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD'] = 'spawn'

IMG1 = "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen-VL/assets/demo.jpeg"
IMG2 = "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen2-VL/assets/demo.jpeg"  # 换成你自己的第二张图
VID  = "https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen2-VL/space_woaudio.mp4"


def prepare_inputs_for_vllm(messages, processor):
    """三件套: prompt + multi_modal_data + mm_processor_kwargs"""
    text = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    image_inputs, video_inputs, video_kwargs = process_vision_info(
        messages,
        image_patch_size=processor.image_processor.patch_size,  # 动态读取, Qwen3-VL 为 16
        return_video_kwargs=True,
        return_video_metadata=True,   # 视频 -> (张量, metadata) 元组列表
    )
    print(f"video_kwargs: {video_kwargs}")   # 预期 {'do_sample_frames': False}

    mm_data = {}
    if image_inputs is not None:
        mm_data['image'] = image_inputs      # PIL 列表直传
    if video_inputs is not None:
        mm_data['video'] = video_inputs      # 元组列表直传, 由 vLLM 解包
    return {
        'prompt': text,
        'multi_modal_data': mm_data,
        'mm_processor_kwargs': video_kwargs, # 防止引擎内二次抽帧
    }


if __name__ == '__main__':
    ckpt = "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct"
    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(ckpt)

    all_messages = [
        [  # 请求 1: 单图
            {"role": "user", "content": [
                {"type": "image", "image": IMG1},
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
            ]},

        [  # 请求 2: 单图
            {"role": "user", "content": [
                {"type": "image", "image": IMG2},
                {"type": "text", "text": "What is in this image?"},

        [  # 请求 3: 视频
            {"role": "user", "content": [
                {"type": "video", "video": VID},
                {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this video."},
            ]},
        ],

    inputs = [prepare_inputs_for_vllm(m, processor) for m in all_messages]

    llm = LLM(model=ckpt, tensor_parallel_size=min(1, torch.cuda.device_count()), seed=0)
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=512)

    outputs = llm.generate(inputs, sampling_params=sampling_params)
    for i, output in enumerate(outputs):
        print("=" * 40)
        print(f"[{i}] prompt 长度: {len(output.prompt_token_ids)} tokens")
        print(f"[{i}] 生成文本: {output.outputs[0].text}")
```

## 6. 本讲小结

- `prepare_inputs_for_vllm` 是仓库级标准模式，在 web 演示、README 示例与全部五个评测目录中逐行同构地出现，核心是三步：`apply_chat_template(tokenize=False)` 渲染文本 → `process_vision_info` 解码视觉素材 → 组装三件套字典。
- 三字段契约：`prompt` 只含占位符的文本串；`multi_modal_data` 按 `'image'`/`'video'` 键挂载现成 PIL/张量数据，且只在模态真实存在时填键；`mm_processor_kwargs` 传递处理器开关。
- Qwen3-VL 视频必须 `return_video_metadata=True`：视频变为 `(张量, metadata)` 元组列表，vLLM 路径直传由引擎解包，transformers 路径才需手动 `zip(*)`；`video_kwargs` 恒含 `do_sample_frames=False`，防止引擎对已采样的帧二次抽帧。
- 引擎与采样：`LLM(...)` 关注张量并行与显存比例，MoE 大模型加 `mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"` 与专家并行；`SamplingParams` 中 `temperature=0` 是评测贪心档，官方 Instruct/Thinking 产品档超参不同。
- vLLM 输出只含新生成部分，直接取 `output.outputs[0].text`，无需 transformers 式的前缀裁剪。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly.     name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.
